Deceased Sh. Mahesh Singh, Husband of Petitioner No.1, father of Petitioner No. 2 and son of Petitioner No.3, died on account of a motor accident which happened on 14.06.2022 at about 09:30 p.m., near Gazipur Subzi Mandi Road near Afcons Company Office.

As a result of which, deceased fell down.
Deceased was taken to LBS Hospital and declared brought dead.
3. On service of notice of the petition, all of the respondents marked appearance filed separate written statement.
3(i). Joint written statement was filed on behalf of R1 & R2.
It is specifically mentioned in their written statement that DAR is incomplete and vague.
It is further submitted that DAR is false _____________________________________________________________ and baseless and the vehicle of R2 has been falsely involved in the present case.

It is further submitted that R2 was having a valid DL at the time of accident and the alleged vehicle was duly insured with R3.
3(ii). R3/Insurer has filed legal offer on its behalf, which was not acceptable to the petitioner.
4. Since the insurance company has given legal offer, apparently the insurance company has admitted its liability and the only question remains to be decided is w.r.t. the quantum of compensation.

Upon completion of pleadings of the parties, following issues were framed vide order dated 17.03.2023:-
i).

The compensation should not be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
ASSESSMENT OF INCOME OF THE DECEASED:
9. PW1 is wife of the deceased and one of the claimants.
It has come in her evidence that deceased was her husband aged 40 years at the time of accident.
She deposed that deceased was a technical person, who knew how to manufacture almirah and how to prepare the dye of Almirah and was earning Rs. 80,000/- per month.
In proof of the economic status of deceased, PW1 had filed on record income tax returns since the year 2018-19, 2019- 20, 2020-21, 2021-2022.
The ITR for the AY 2020-21 bears the stamp of invalid everywhere and there is no explanation for it and hence, this document cannot be considered.
The ITR for the AY- 2018-19 & 2019-20 are incomplete and hence not being considered.

The ITR for the AY- 2021-22 reflects that the same was submitted on 16.08.2021 by deceased himself and as per the same, the gross annual income was Rs.4,50,230/-
and the income tax payable was Rs.7012/- and thus the annual income can be taken to be Rs.4,32,018/-.
Petitioners have not filed educational documents of the deceased.
No bank account statement of the deceased is filed either.
Hence, on the basis of the latest ITR for AY-2021-22, his income on the date of accident i.e. 14.06.2022 is considered to be Rs.36,935/- per month.

sentences.text: In the claim petition, the LRs of the deceased have claimed the age of the deceased to be 42 years.
The claim petition is supported with affidavit of the petitioners.
Further, in the postmortem report of the deceased Mahesh Singh, his age is mentioned as 42 years.
In the copy of computation for ITR of the deceased, as filed by the petitioner for the AY 2021-22, the date of birth of deceased Mahesh Singh is shown as 03.05.1981.
In the Aadhar card, the date of birth of deceased is mentioned as 15.02.1982.
However, in view of the claim in the petition duly supported by the affidavit of the petitioners, the age of the deceased is mentioned as 42 year old on the date of accident.
The ITR document shows the date of birth as 03.05.1981 and ITR is stated to have been submitted by deceased himself.
No election ID card, birth certificate and any other document in proof of age has been filed on record.
Hence, his date of birth is taken as 03.05.1981.

In case title "Saroj & Ors. Vs. IFFCO TOKIO GIC & Ors. 2024 INSC 816 ", it has been observed by Hon'ble Apex Court that Aadhar Card should only be treated as proof of identity and not as definitive proof of date of birth.

FUTURE PROSPECTS:
11.
This issue was considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pranay Sethi & Others (Supra).

Relevant parts of the judgment are reproduced here as under:
"(iii) While determining the income, an addition of 50% of actual salary to the i n c o m e o f t h e d e c e a s e d t o w a r d s f u t u r e _____________________________________________________________ prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30%, if the age of the deceased was between 40 to 50 years.

In case the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years,
the addition should be 15%.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.
(iv) In case the deceased was self- employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.
An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."
12. The deceased can be presumed to be as self-employed.
Since the deceased Sh. Mahesh Kumar was 41 years old, 25% future prospects has to be granted.
DEDUCTION TOWARDS PERSONAL LIVING EXPENSES:
13. After choosing the age, multiplier and income of the deceased, necessary deductions have to be made out of the income of the deceased towards her personal expenses.

Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Reshma Kumari & Ors. v. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65, in para 30, laid down the necessary deductions towards personal living and expenses of deceased as under :
_____________________________________________________________ Deductions out of earning of the Number of deceased dependents Married Persons Where dependent is 1 Half Where the number of dependent family 1/3rd members is 2 to 3 Where the number of dependent family 1/4th members is 4 to 6 Where the number of dependent family 1/5th members exceeds 6 (six) Deductions out of earning of the deceased Number of dependents Bachelor In case family is not large Half
